metaTitle: JPEG vs PNG: Which Format Is Better for Photos and Graphics?
metaDescription: Learn when to use JPEG vs PNG for photos, graphics, transparency, and web delivery. The guide explains real-world tradeoffs and links to the right tool.

guideContent.section1Title: Why JPEG and PNG are still the most important format decisions
guideContent.section1Body: JPEG is usually the best fit for photos and everyday sharing because it balances quality and size well. PNG is stronger when graphics need transparency, crisp edges, or repeated editing. The best choice depends on the destination of the file and the kind of detail that matters most.
guideContent.section2Title: When to choose each format in practical workflows
guideContent.section2Body: Professional teams usually choose JPEG for photos and screenshots that need broad compatibility. They choose PNG when a logo, icon, overlay, or transparent asset needs to stay editable and predictable across apps. The strongest workflow tests the output in the actual destination before it is published.
steps: Start by deciding whether the image is primarily photographic or graphic.
Choose JPEG for general photo use and PNG when transparency or editing flexibility matters.
Test the output in the place where it will be used before you publish or share it.

faqs.question: Which format is better for photos?
faqs.answer: JPEG is usually the better default for photos because it keeps file sizes practical and is widely supported.

faqs.question: When should I choose PNG?
faqs.answer: PNG is the better choice for logos, icons, screenshots, and any asset that needs transparency or repeated editing.

faqs.question: Can I convert between these formats safely?
faqs.answer: Yes. The workflow stays local in the browser, so you can convert between formats without uploading the file to a remote service.
